learning: Iteration 2 showed the ±0.06 span removed line losses but left max_error at the 0.061 floor and cut slalom progress from 0.110 to 0.035. A steady mismatch-driven offset is the leading explanation, so this race tests the integral term alongside the wider track.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's wheel_track 0.12 proposal on the ±0.06 m span. Controller changes only ki (0.05 to 0.5) to test whether integral action removes the steady drift that holds max_error at 0.061.
rationale: Iteration 2 kept line losses at 0 with the ±0.06 m span, but max_error stayed at 0.0609 to 0.0614 on every track, which is the 0.06 m off-track limit being crossed. Oval progress was 0.115 in all three designs, so the first bend is still the failure point. Slalom progress fell from 0.105 (iteration 1, ±0.04 m) to 0.035, so the wider span hurt slalom while fixing line loss. The uniform ~0.061 floor across tracks, plus the fixed left/right motor mismatch in the simulator, points to a steady lateral drift. With kp alone, a constant mismatch leaves a steady offset of mismatch/kp. ki = 0.05 is far too small to remove it. The Builder's proposal is wheel_track 0.12 with the span, footprint and y row unchanged, which raises turn authority for the same wheel difference. I accept that geometry unchanged. On the controller side I raise ki from 0.05 to 0.5 so the integral (clamped at ±2, so at most ±1 turn) can cancel the constant drift. I keep kp at 2.5 rather than cutting it, because slalom oscillation was 0.159 at ±0.04 m and the wider span raises edge gain, but the integral is expected to remove the offset without adding much jitter. kd 0.15, base_speed 1.6 and last_direction are unchanged so this race isolates ki and the 0.12 m track. Expected: max_error below about 0.055 on oval and s-bend, and oval progress past 0.115. If max_error still sits at 0.061, drift is not the mismatch offset and the next step is wheel_track or wheel_radius rather than ki.
